title: The Top 5 Contract Exclusions And What Endurance Covers | Endurance Warranty
summary: A warranty seller's own blog pitches its maintenance and roadside add-ons while explaining the standard exclusions every contract carries.

assertions.quote: up to $3,500 per year in maintenance benefits, including oil and filter changes, tire rotations

verdicts.note: Bundling a maintenance allowance into a protection plan is a real, verifiable product feature in this market segment, though the specific dollar figure is the vendor's own unverified claim.

assertions.quote: standard benefits like 24/7 roadside assistance, towing, rental car coverage, and trip interruption protection

verdicts.note: Roadside assistance and rental-car benefits are standard inclusions across most vehicle service contracts, independent of any one vendor.

assertions.quote: Routine maintenance work and wear-and-tear parts are almost always excluded from coverage.

verdicts.note: Excluding wear items and routine maintenance is near-universal in vehicle service contracts and is confirmed by FTC consumer guidance.

assertions.quote: almost every extended car warranty excludes any problems that existed before you bought the coverage

verdicts.note: Waiting periods and pre-existing-condition exclusions are standard, contract-defined features across the industry.

assertions.quote: if a covered water pump failure cooks your head gasket, some contracts will pay only for the pump itself, not the additional damage

verdicts.note: Denying a claim because the proximate cause traces to an excluded part is a documented, common exclusion mechanism, corroborated independently by a mechanic's own claim-denial account.

assertions.quote: Take advantage of our 30-day money-back guarantee!

verdicts.note: Short cancellation windows are commonly advertised, but consumer complaints and trade coverage show cancellation and refund processes are often made slow or difficult in practice.
